tokyo3_rice_hack.gf_detail: Fully dedicated 100% gluten-free bakery — there is NO wheat flour on the premises. Everything is baked from rice flour (specially grown Koshihikari, rice bran included), natural yeast, kibi sugar and rock salt. Findmeglutenfree lists it explicitly as a "Dedicated Gluten-Free Bakery," and a celiac reviewer (celiacchat.ca) reported no cross-contamination concerns and that the owner/staff understand celiac disease. Signature curry pan is baked, not deep-fried, so there is no shared-fryer risk. One of the safest bakery options in Tokyo for a celiac. Caveat: savory items (curry fillings, cheese/mayo/shirasu toppings) — confirm the individual filling if avoiding anything beyond gluten, and tell staff "celiac" so they handle it cleanly.
tokyo3_rice_hack.vegan_detail: Not a vegan-only shop, but it carries genuine vegan items among the gluten-free lineup: a chickpea vegan curry pan (¥360), a big vegan marinara/margherita-style rice-crust pizza, and several plain bread rolls/loaves and an "ichizen no pan" with a meat-free bolognese/stew. Many other items are NOT vegan — cheese curry pan, cheese-stuffed rolls, and a wafu pizza topped with cheese, mayo and shirasu (whitebait). Egg/dairy are used in some breads. No bonito/dashi is central to a bakery, but savory fillings should be confirmed. Ask which loaves of the day are egg- and dairy-free; the vegan curry pan and vegan pizza are the reliable picks.

chef_bio.background: Otsuka Setsuko is widely known in Japan as the "Mother of Rice Flour" (米粉の母), a leading figure in the domestic rice-flour movement who is regularly featured in media. She produced and launched RICE HACK Gluten-free Bakery, which opened on November 12, 2022 in Jingumae, Shibuya, operated through 株式会社ライステラス (Rice Terrace / Onden House).
chef_bio.philosophy: That Japanese rice "can change the world" — her breads are not meant as mere wheat substitutes but as foods delicious enough that people with celiac disease or wheat allergy and people without can enjoy the exact same thing together. She emphasizes rice flour's own nutritional properties (rice bran, whole-grain character) rather than mimicking wheat.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour bread and gluten-free baking — the shop's signature is a fully from-scratch baked curry pan (homemade curry filling and rice-flour breadcrumbs, crisped in the oven rather than deep-fried).

tokyo3_a_375.gf_detail: The official site advertises a new menu line explicitly labeled "グルテンフリー・五葷抜き" (gluten-free & no five-pungent-vegetables), so real GF dishes exist and the staff will engage with the request. However this is NOT a dedicated GF kitchen: it is an omnivore macrobiotic kitchen that also fries vegemeat karaage/tempura (wheat batter) and serves fish/game, so shared-fryer and shared-surface wheat cross-contact is likely. A celiac must specifically ask whether the GF items use wheat-free tamari — standard Japanese shoyu (and therefore most sauces, teriyaki-style glazes, and the tsuyu for any noodle/sushi dish) contains wheat. The macrobiotic base (brown rice, miso, vegetables) is naturally low-gluten but miso and soy sauce are the wheat risks to verify. No dedicated fryer confirmed. Treat as "real GF options, celiac should confirm dish-by-dish," not a safe dedicated environment.
tokyo3_a_375.vegan_detail: Clearly marked, abundant vegan menu ("ビーガンメニューあり") built on macrobiotic principles: vegemeat karaage, tofu steak, vegan sushi, vegetable curry, plus brown rice / miso soup / vegetable sets. Additive-free, naturally-cultivated ("自然栽培・無添加") ingredients. Because the same kitchen also cooks fish (e.g. Norwegian mackerel) and venison, it is not an exclusively vegan house — confirm your dish is the vegan version. Hidden-dashi caution: no source explicitly states the miso soup / broths are bonito-free; macrobiotic kitchens typically use kombu (kelp) dashi, but ask to confirm plant-based dashi. Staff invite vegetarians and allergy diners to speak up ("ベジタリアンの方や、アレルギーの方もお気軽にお申し出ください").

He runs a YouTube channel ('もみの木チャンネル') and personally sources grains and vegetables from natural-cultivation (自然栽培) farms.
chef_bio.philosophy: Cooking rooted in macrobiotics (玄米菜食) — whole brown rice, vegetables, fermented foods, additive-free ('無添加') seasonings and 'electronic ion water' — with gentle seasoning meant to be kind to the body. He verifies each farm's soil and water 'with his five senses' ('土、水など栽培環境のすべてを五感で確認') and has a stated ambition to help shift Japanese agriculture toward natural cultivation.
chef_bio.specialty: Macrobiotic / plant-forward natural food: vegemeat karaage, tofu steak, vegan sushi and brown-rice sets, alongside naturally-raised fish and game for non-vegetarian guests.

anecdotes.text: Founded MOMINOKI HOUSE in 1976 near Killer-dori in Jingumae; described as one of Japan's oldest natural-food restaurants, running 40-plus years under the same owner-chef.

tokyo_kyushu_jangara_ginza.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The company describes its ramen noodles as a blend of several wheat flours bound with egg white, and lists no gluten-free noodle. Its FAQ publishes no allergen information. The vegan bowl is seasoned with dark soy sauce (濃い口醤油), which in Japan is brewed with wheat by default, and the seasoned egg is marinated in the house soy sauce. Not suitable for celiacs.
tokyo_kyushu_jangara_ginza.vegan_detail: The Ginza shop lists one plant-based bowl, 濃い口醤油のヴィーガンらあめん (vegan dark-soy-sauce ramen): a vegetable soup with a deep soy sauce flavour, which can be ordered without the 'five pungent vegetables' (garlic, onion, leek and the like). At the Akihabara branch the same bowl is documented with egg-free noodles and soy-meat chashu; ask at Ginza that it is made the same way. Every other bowl is built on pork-bone soup (with chicken frames in the house Kyushu Jangara), and the plant-based bowl comes out of the same kitchen.
tokyo_kyushu_jangara_ginza.hours_raw: 11:00–22:30 (last order 22:15) per the shop's own page, which names no closed day. Tabelog's listing gives Mon–Sat 11:00–22:00 and closed Sundays — confirm before a Sunday visit.
tokyo_kyushu_jangara_ginza.notes: [Ramen · Tokyo chain] The Ginza branch of Kyushu Jangara, a Tokyo ramen company founded in Akihabara in 1984. It opened on Mihara-dōri in Ginza 7-chōme in 1991 and moved to this spot on 2010-07-07. Its 16 seats are all at tables. The house bowl is a mild pork-bone soup with chicken frames and vegetables. The rest of the line-up runs from the creamy Hakata/Kurume-style Bonshan to the Kumamoto-style Kobonshan with black-garlic oil. The 'zenbu-iri' (everything in) bowl, with braised pork belly, mentaiko and a seasoned egg, is a phrase the shop says was born at its own counter. Pickled mustard greens and red ginger are free at the table. There is also a plant-based shoyu ramen. Menus in English, Chinese, Korean and Thai are kept at every branch, and 2026 diners describe a queue of overseas visitors at peak times.

roles: ramen company (タスグループ — 九州じゃんがら)
chef_bio.origin: Founded in Akihabara, Tokyo, in 1984; Kyushu-style tonkotsu
chef_bio.background: Kyushu Jangara is run by Tas Group (タスグループ), which began in 1979 as the ブルカン塾 cram school and opened its first ramen shop in Akihabara in 1984, in the company's words to shore up the school's finances. It now runs five Kyushu Jangara shops in Tokyo — Akihabara, Harajuku, Ginza, Akasaka and Shiba-Daimon — plus a vegan bistro in Harajuku, and in 1993 moved its prep into a central kitchen.
chef_bio.specialty: Mild tonkotsu (Kyushu Jangara), creamy Hakata/Kurume-rooted Bonshan, Kumamoto-style Kobonshan with house black-garlic oil; zenbu-iri toppings; a plant-based shoyu ramen.

anecdotes.text: The company started as a cram school (ブルカン塾, 1979); it opened Kyushu Jangara in 1984 to rebuild the school's finances (「ブルカン塾」の経営基盤を立て直すために).
The Ginza shop first opened in 1991 on Mihara-dōri in Ginza 7-chōme.
It moved to its present address, Ginza 6-12-17, on 7 July 2010.

'Zenbu-iri' (全部入り) — braised pork belly, mentaiko and a seasoned egg on one bowl — is a word the shop says was born at its counter in 1984, when customers asked which toppings they wanted answered 'put everything in!'
The braised pork belly (角肉) is a recipe handed down from a master of Nagasaki shippoku cuisine.
The illustrated postcard pictures (絵手紙) on the shop walls are the work of the company president, Shimokawa Takashi.

The vegan ramen grew out of offers from several Southeast Asian countries from 2013, was served in JAL international first and business class, and has been on the menu at every Kyushu Jangara in several variations since 2015.
A June 2026 diner singled out the manager's friendliness and the energetic way the staff served a queue of overseas visitors.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式サイト(kyushujangara.co.jp)より: タスグループ(代表取締役社長 下川高士、設立1979年9月)。1979年ブルカン塾、1984年九州じゃんがら秋葉原本店創業。銀座店は1991年に銀座七丁目の三原通りに開店(沿革)、食べログによれば2010年7月7日に銀座7-11-10から現住所(銀座6-12-17 銀座片桐ビル1F)へ移転。営業時間11:00〜22:30(L.O.22:15)、お会計は退店時レジ、現金・交通系IC・PayPay・Alipay・WeChat Pay・各種カード。銀座店のメニュー: 九州じゃんがら、ぼんしゃん、こぼんしゃん、九州じゃんがら味噌、からぼん、濃い口醤油のヴィーガンらあめん。麺は数種類の小麦粉と卵白。英語・中国語・韓国語・タイ語メニューを全店に用意(よくあるご質問)。

cultural_comfort.note: The company keeps English, Chinese, Korean and Thai menus at every shop, and 2026 diners describe a mostly overseas crowd. Table seating only; pay at the register on the way out (cards, IC cards and QR payments accepted). Expect a queue at peak times.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The ramen noodles are a blend of several wheat flours bound with egg white (数種類の小麦粉の配合と、卵白); no gluten-free noodle is offered.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The plant-based bowl is a dark-soy-sauce (濃い口醤油) ramen; Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat unless stated otherwise.
The seasoned egg (味玉子) is marinated in the house soy-sauce tare.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The house soup is pork bone and chicken frames simmered with vegetables; Bonshan is pork-bone-led and Kobonshan pork bone and chicken.
At the Akihabara branch the vegan bowl is documented with a vegetable-only soup, egg-free noodles and soy-meat chashu — confirm the Ginza bowl is made the same way.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The company FAQ publishes no allergen or ingredient information.

positives.text: A permanent plant-based shoyu ramen on the Ginza menu, orderable without the five pungent vegetables (五葷抜き).

tokyo_chuka_ginza_tei.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. This is a neighbourhood Chinese counter (machi-chūka) built around ramen, tsukemen, gyoza and stir-fries. The ramen-type noodles are wheat by default, and no gluten-free noodle or dish is mentioned in any source. The house miso tare is made in-house, and its miso type is not published (miso can be barley). The gyoza come with a vinegar-and-soy dip. The rice dishes and stir-fries are not documented ingredient by ingredient. One tiny kitchen does all of it. Not suitable for celiacs.
tokyo_chuka_ginza_tei.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The owner says one house soup, made from chicken feet (もみじ), pig's trotters and vegetables, is the base of every noodle dish. The signature dishes are pork-heavy: miso chashu, the minced-meat mapo harusame rice bowl and twice-cooked pork. No vegetarian or vegan dish is mentioned in any source.
tokyo_chuka_ginza_tei.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–01:30 (the 2023 interview gives last order 01:15). Closed Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays and the days before and after a public holiday. The shop says it may close after lunch in midsummer heat, so call ahead (03-3571-6450). Cash only; no reservations.
tokyo_chuka_ginza_tei.notes: [Mom & Pop · machi-chūka] A 1975 neighbourhood Chinese counter on Hanatsubaki-dōri, run by the founder's family into its third generation. The grandfather left an office job, trained at the 1970s tsukemen chain つけ麺大王 (Tsukemen Daiō) and opened a franchise of it here; around 1977 he went independent as 銀座亭. Tsukemen is still the oldest dish on the menu. Set meals were added for the people who work Ginza's nights, and today orders run about six set meals to three noodle dishes to one drinking snack. Five or six cooks work the wok behind a U-shaped counter of 15 seats. Diners come for the miso chashu and the mapo harusame rice bowl. Tabelog named it one of Tokyo's 100 best Chinese restaurants (百名店) in 2024 and 2026. Expect a queue at peak times; staff hand over a picture menu on request.

roles: third-generation owner
runs the shop with his father (second generation)
chef_bio.origin: Ginza 7-chōme, Tokyo — founded in 1975 by his grandfather
chef_bio.background: Kitaoka's grandfather left a salaried job, trained at つけ麺大王 and opened this counter in 1975 as one of its franchises, then went independent around 1977 under the name 銀座亭. Kitaoka worked at a yakitori restaurant before joining his father at the shop in 2020; they had expected the Tokyo Olympics to make the shop busy that year.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「これからも『銀座亭』が提供してきた、食べて安心する味を守っていきたい」 — to keep serving the comforting food the shop has always served.
chef_bio.specialty: Miso chashu ramen (wok-fried vegetables, four thick slices of pork shoulder); mapo harusame rice bowl; tsukemen descended from the つけ麺大王 recipe.

anecdotes.text: The shop opened in 1975 as a franchise of つけ麺大王 — 「実は、創業当時の屋号は『つけ麺大王』だったんですよね」 — and became 銀座亭 around 1977.
Set meals were added, Kitaoka believes, because the black-suited men of Ginza's night trade and the area's restaurant workers do more physical work than it looks: 「スタミナをつけられるようにという想いで」.
Five or six cooks share the narrow kitchen. The miso chashu came out in under five minutes: bean sprouts and pork belly fired in the wok, then soup and the house miso tare added in the same pan.
Kitaoka reckons there are only about three machi-chūka left in Ginza, his included, and says some customers from his grandfather's day still come in.
Selected for Tabelog Chinese TOKYO "Tabelog 100" (百名店) in 2024 and again in 2026.
An October 2026 diner noted the cash-only sign, that staff checked before serving two rice dishes to one person, and that they produced a picture menu when asked.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: さんたつ(2023.11.10)より: 1975年創業の町中華。祖父が脱サラし『つけ麺大王』で修業、フランチャイズで開業、1977年ごろ独立して『銀座亭』に。3代目店主・北岡秋平さん(元焼き鳥店勤務、2020年から父と)。コの字カウンター、厨房に5〜6人。スープはもみじ・豚足・野菜で麺類すべてを賄う。自家製味噌だれは少し辛味。みそチャーシュー1300円(豚肩ロースのチャーシュー4枚、中太ストレート麺)。注文は定食6・麺3・つまみ1。住所 中央区銀座7-11-10、営業11:30〜翌1:15LO、土日休。食べログ: 中国料理 百名店 2024・2026、15席(カウンターのみ)、現金のみ、予約不可、平日11:30〜翌1:30、土日祝・祝前日・祝後日休。

cultural_comfort.note: A cramped, fast 15-seat counter; cash only, no reservations, and a queue at peak times. The menu is Japanese, but staff hand over a picture menu on request. Tabelog asks families with children to come between about 14:30 and 18:00, outside the rush.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Every noodle dish is served from one shared house soup, and everything is cooked by five or six cooks in one small wok kitchen; no gluten-free noodle or dish is mentioned.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The miso chashu uses a house-made, slightly spicy miso tare added to the soup in the wok; the type of miso is not stated (barley miso contains gluten).
The gyoza are served with a vinegar-and-soy-sauce dip with chili oil.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The soup — chicken feet (もみじ), pig's trotters and vegetables — is the base of every noodle dish (麺類のメニューはこれですべてを賄う).
The signature mapo harusame rice bowl is packed with minced meat.

tokyo_ginza_tanmen.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The shop serves one dish, tanmen: thin, straight ramen-type noodles, which are wheat by default, in a salted chicken-frame soup. No gluten-free noodle is mentioned in any source. Not suitable for celiacs.
tokyo_ginza_tanmen.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The only dish is tanmen, a chicken-frame (鶏ガラ) soup with napa cabbage and pork. No meat-free version is mentioned in any source.
tokyo_ginza_tanmen.hours_raw: Mon–Thu 11:30–15:00 & 17:00–20:00 (last order 19:30); Fri 11:30–15:00 only. Closed Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays. Ticket machine; cash only.
tokyo_ginza_tanmen.notes: [Mom & Pop · tanmen] A 9-seat counter near Kabuki-za that has served exactly one dish since it opened in January 2019. The owner taught themself to make it, trying to recreate a tanmen they used to eat as a student. The bowl is a clear, salted chicken-frame soup with thin straight noodles, buried under napa cabbage and a little pork. The cabbage is simmered with the soup in a frying pan, but only so far that it stays crunchy. The shop buys whatever napa cabbage is best that season and posts its origin, which in 2026 was Nagano's Nobeyama and Saku-Asama highlands. Toppings are butter, cilantro and nori. Homemade chili oil, white pepper and vinegar sit on the counter. A September 2026 diner found the owner running the shop alone. Lunch queues are common.

roles: owner-operator
chef_bio.background: The owner set out to recreate the tanmen they used to eat as a student and worked it out by self-study (独学で研究), opening this one-dish counter in 2019. No other branch was found.
chef_bio.specialty: Tanmen: salted chicken-frame soup, thin straight noodles, a mound of seasonal napa cabbage and pork.

anecdotes.text: 「店主が、学生時代に食べていた「たんめん」の味を作れたらと独学で研究」 — the owner studied on their own to recreate the tanmen of their student days.

The napa cabbage is whatever is best that season; at the time of the interview it was Yūki city's brand cabbage 「ゆうきくん」, yellow-hearted, soft and sweet. It is simmered with the soup in a frying pan, but only so far that it keeps its crunch.
The shop posts where the day's cabbage is from — Saku-Asama highland cabbage in July 2026, Nobeyama's in August and September, whose sweetness the shop's notice credited to morning dew and mist.
Order less noodles and the staff offer to add more cabbage instead; butter comes chilled and sliced on its own plate, and stays firm so you add it bit by bit.
A September 2026 diner found the owner running the counter alone.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: FRaU(2025年2月15日、宇賀なつみ)より: 「銀座たんめん」は東銀座駅すぐのたんめん専門店。メニューはたんめんのみ、カウンター席のみ。店主が学生時代に食べたたんめんの味を独学で研究。鶏ガラベースの塩味スープに白菜と豚肉のみ。たんめん1000円(当時)。白菜は時期のいいもの(取材時は結城市「ゆうきくん」)、フライパンでスープと煮込みシャキシャキ感を残す。なっぷ: 2019年オープン、カウンター9席、細めのストレート麺、卓上に自家製ラー油。食べログ: 2019年1月16日オープン、9席、現金のみ、月〜木11:30〜15:00/17:00〜20:00(L.O.19:30)、金11:30〜15:00、土日祝休。

cultural_comfort.note: Order at a Japanese ticket machine. The choice is just tanmen or large tanmen plus a few toppings, so it is easy to manage. A 9-seat counter with lunch queues; cash only.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The one dish is tanmen — thin straight noodles in a salted chicken-frame soup; no gluten-free noodle is offered.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The soup is chicken-frame based (鶏ガラベース) and the only toppings are napa cabbage and pork.

tokyo_ramen_matsutomi_ginza.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. Ramen, tantanmen, tsukemen, gyoza and shumai. There are three kinds of wheat noodle (egg noodles, thin straight, thick), soy sauce and grated garlic are on the counter, and every noodle soup shares one base stock. No gluten-free dish is mentioned in any source.
tokyo_ramen_matsutomi_ginza.vegan_detail: The shop's own Tabelog listing ticks 'vegetarian options', but no source says what they are. Every noodle dish (shoyu ramen, tantanmen, clam ramen) shares one base soup of pork bones (げん骨) and Hidaka kombu, so none of them is vegan. The side dishes include morokyu (cucumber with miso). Ask the staff what they mean by the vegetarian option.
tokyo_ramen_matsutomi_ginza.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–15:00 & 17:00–04:00; Sat 11:00–15:00 & 18:00–22:00; closed Sundays and holidays. Cash only; a service charge is added. Free large noodles at lunch.
tokyo_ramen_matsutomi_ginza.notes: [Mom & Pop · ramen izakaya] A Ginza back-lane ramen shop open since 1996, until 4 a.m. on weekdays: lunch for office workers and shoppers, a last bowl after drinks, and early-morning ramen. Iwano Tsutomu trained in about three ramen shops, joined Matsutomi in 2000 and took it over from the founder in 2013. He keeps the founder's base soup of pork bones and Hidaka kombu, which goes into every bowl. The most popular is shoyu ramen. The quiet favourite is the clam ramen, limited to 20 a day, made with clams bought fresh each morning and served with butter, kombu and egg noodles. At night it becomes a ramen izakaya, with a cheap drink set and the 特許しうまい, a shumai made by a patented method. Cash only.

roles: owner (second generation, since 2013)
chef_bio.background: Iwano had always wanted his own ramen shop. He worked in about three ramen shops to study how each made its soup, joined Matsutomi at around 25 in 2000, and took it over from the founder in 2013. Long-serving staff help him keep the founder's recipes.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「先代が作った味をそのまま受け継いでます」 — keeping the founder's flavour, changing it little by little and adding new dishes, and carrying the shop on for another ten or twenty years.
chef_bio.specialty: Shoyu ramen and clam ramen on a pork-bone and Hidaka-kombu base; tantanmen; patented shumai and gyoza.

anecdotes.text: Three noodles for three styles: egg noodles for the clam ramen, thin straight noodles for shoyu ramen, thick noodles for tsukemen.
The clam ramen (20 a day) uses clams bought at market every morning, with cut kombu, sesame and a pat of butter that turns it into a clam-butter soup.
The 特許しうまい holds a patent on its ingredient ratios and mixing method — pork with prawn and crab.
「常連さんのお陰でコロナも乗り越えてきました」 — the regulars carried the shop through the pandemic.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: さんたつ(2023.11.17): らーめん松富、1996年創業、2013年に創業者から岩野努さんが継承(2000年から勤務)。基本スープはげん骨・北海道日高昆布など、醤油らーめん・担々麺・あさりらーめん共通。あさりらーめん900円(当時)・1日20食、特許しうまい夜2個360円・昼セット270円。17席。食べログ: 15席、現金のみ、サービス料あり、英語メニューあり、ベジタリアンメニューあり(店舗情報)、持ち帰り(餃子・しうまい)。

cultural_comfort.note: A casual back-lane counter; Tabelog notes an English menu. Cash only. Busy at lunch and late at night.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Three wheat noodles in use (egg noodles, thin straight, thick); gyoza and shumai are on the menu.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The most popular bowl is shoyu ramen; Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat unless stated otherwise.
Soy sauce, vinegar, chili oil and grated garlic are on the counter.

vegan_cross_contact.text: 「基本のスープは醤油らーめんも担々麺もあさりらーめんも同じで、げん骨や北海道の日高昆布とか」 — one pork-bone and kombu base for every bowl.

tokyo_ginza_hachigo.gf_detail: Not gluten-free, although there is no soy-sauce tare: the soup is seasoned only with a little Guérande salt. The noodles are a special wheat-flour-and-kansui noodle from Asakusa Kaikarō, and the signature bowl adds ravioli. No gluten-free noodle is offered.
tokyo_ginza_hachigo.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The soup is duck frames and duck thigh, a whole Nagoya Cochin chicken, prosciutto and scallop, with kombu, dried shiitake and dried tomato. Every bowl carries pork chashu, and the signature ravioli contain foie gras.
tokyo_ginza_hachigo.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 11:00 until the soup runs out (Tabelog lists 11:00–16:00). Closed Mondays, plus some Tuesdays (check the shop's social media). Walk-ins from 11:00 in order of arrival; from 12:00 reservations take priority. Reservations open every Saturday at 9:00 for the following week (TableCheck only) and carry a ¥500 seat fee.
tokyo_ginza_hachigo.notes: [Ramen · French-chef chuka soba] Matsumura Yasushi spent 36 years in French kitchens, including as executive chef of Kyoto's ANA hotel, then turned to ramen to serve 'a full course in a bowl'. After his 勝本 shops in Suidōbashi and Jimbōchō, he opened this 6-seat counter in December 2018. He spent months after fit-out perfecting the bowl. The soup uses no tare: a golden consommé of duck, whole Nagoya Cochin chicken, prosciutto and scallop with kombu, shiitake and dried tomato, seasoned only with a little Guérande salt. It is paired with a thin noodle made for this soup by Asakusa Kaikarō. Tabelog has named it a ramen 百名店 every year from 2019 to 2025, and the 2026 Michelin Guide gave it a seventh straight listing (Bib Gourmand). The name refers to the 8.5-tsubo room and to a mountaineering saying about the eighth station. Book on TableCheck or queue. The owner and staff speak English.

roles: owner-chef
company: 株式会社Food Operation Japan (also runs the 勝本 shops)
chef_bio.origin: French cuisine — 36 years, incl. executive chef at Kyoto ANA Hotel (now ANA Crowne Plaza Kyoto)
chef_bio.background: After 36 years as a French chef, Matsumura decided to recreate 'a full course in a bowl' and switched to ramen. He opened 中華そば勝本 in Suidōbashi (March 2015) and つけそば神田勝本 in Jimbōchō (February 2016), and the group now also has 豊洲勝本. Ginza Hachigō, opened in December 2018, is where he put everything he knew. Turning 66 in October 2025, he said he hopes to stay at the stove as long as he can, and has an eye on opening abroad.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「誰でも気取らず美味しい料理を手軽に楽しんでいただきたい」 — anyone should be able to enjoy fine food casually.
chef_bio.specialty: Tare-free golden consommé chuka soba; ravioli of truffle, foie gras and prosciutto; Kaikarō thin noodles; pepper-caviar chashu.

anecdotes.text: The name has two sources: the 8.5-tsubo shop, and 「八合目まで登っても、まだ五合目と心得よ」 — even at the eighth station, think of yourself as at the fifth.
After the shop was finished he kept it shut for several months, still working on the ideal bowl.
The noodles were designed for this soup by Asakusa Kaikarō's noodle-maker 不死鳥カラス, blended so they do not go soft or cloud the soup.
A seventh consecutive Michelin listing (Bib Gourmand) in the Michelin Guide Tokyo 2026.
After the bowl, a cold-brewed hōjicha.
An October 2026 diner found the owner friendly and fluent in English; another was guided by an English-speaking member of staff.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Food Operation Japanプレスリリース(2025.9.26): 店主松村康史、京都全日空ホテル総料理長などフレンチ36年。2015年中華そば勝本(水道橋)、2016年つけそば神田勝本(神保町)、2018年12月銀座 八五。タレ不使用、生ハム等の旨味の黄金スープ、浅草開化楼の特製細麺。ミシュランガイド東京2026ビブグルマン、7年連続。系列: 中華そば勝本、中華そば豊洲勝本、つけそば神田勝本。enjoytokyo(2019): 鴨ガラ・鴨モモ肉・名古屋コーチン丸鶏・生ハム、イタヤガイ・ドライトマト・昆布・干し椎茸、微量のゲラント塩。カウンター6席。食べログ: 百名店2019–2025、予約は毎週土曜9時TableCheck、予約者席料500円。

cultural_comfort.note: The owner and staff speak English (2026 reviews), and many guests are from overseas. Six counter seats, quiet classical music, no condiments on the counter. Reservations (TableCheck, Saturday 9:00 for the next week) carry a ¥500 seat fee; walk-ins queue from 11:00.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The noodles are a special wheat-flour-and-kansui noodle from Asakusa Kaikarō (小麦粉とかん水の配合).

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No tare is used: the soup is seasoned with a trace of Guérande salt (微量のゲラント塩) and prosciutto rather than soy sauce.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Duck frames, duck thigh, a whole Nagoya Cochin chicken and prosciutto, with itaya scallop, dried tomato, kombu and dried shiitake.

tokyo_chukasoba_kyoraku.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. One shoyu chuka soba is the base of every bowl. The noodles and the wonton skins are made in-house from wheat, and the menma and chashu are seasoned. No gluten-free option is mentioned.
tokyo_chukasoba_kyoraku.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The single soup is chicken and niboshi (dried sardine) finished with soy sauce, and the toppings are pork chashu and meat-filled wontons.
tokyo_chukasoba_kyoraku.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 11:00–17:30; Sat 11:00–16:00; closed Wednesdays, Sundays and holidays (Tabelog; the 2023 interview gave 11:00–18:00 and closed Sun/holidays). Cash only — Kiyoko, the owner's mother, takes your order and buys the ticket for you.
tokyo_chukasoba_kyoraku.notes: [Mom & Pop · since 1956] A three-generation Ginza chuka-soba shop. Founder Nakano Taichirō started with a street stall and set up in Ginza 2-chōme in 1956. His grandson Kazuhiko, who trained in Cantonese kitchens, now runs it with his parents Kikuo and Kiyoko. When the building was rebuilt, the shop closed from 2016 to 2019. Its noodle maker retired around then, so Kazuhiko learned the craft and now makes the noodles and wonton skins in-house; the noodles are made after closing, sometimes until 2 a.m. There is one shoyu soup, chicken and niboshi, under every bowl. The wonton-men is the favourite, and the menma is rehydrated over four days. The name 共楽 means a happy life shared by the house and its customers. Twelve seats, a queue at opening, cash only.

roles: third-generation owner
with 二代目 中野喜久雄 (father) and 中野きよ子 (mother)
chef_bio.origin: Ginza 2-chōme; founded 1956 by 中野太一郎, who began with a street stall
chef_bio.background: Kazuhiko helped in the shop from primary school, trained in Cantonese restaurants from 20, and joined at 26 when his father asked. During the 2016–2019 rebuild of the building he worked in other ramen shops to learn noodle-making, and on reopening in 2019 switched both the noodles and the wonton skins to house-made.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「お客様が喜んでくれて、また来てくれるのが一番」. The founder chose the name 共楽 hoping the owners and customers would share a happy life.
chef_bio.specialty: Shoyu chuka soba (chicken and niboshi); wonton-men with house-made skins; chashu of pork thigh; four-day menma.

anecdotes.text: The founder, 中野太一郎, began with a ramen stall and opened in Ginza 2-chōme; he died in 1999 at 89.
Prep starts at 8 a.m.; after closing, Kazuhiko makes the noodles, sometimes until 2 a.m. In service his father works the kitchen and he sometimes takes the floor — 「父とはあんまりしゃべらないですね」.
Dried menma is rehydrated over four days before seasoning; the chashu is pork thigh (もも).
When you go to buy a wonton-men ticket, Kiyoko takes your order and buys it for you — a courtesy the shop has always kept.
A Fukusuke figure has watched over the shop since the founder's day.
An October 2026 diner: the elderly owner smiled and thanked them on the way out.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: さんたつ(2023.10.17): 共楽、1956年創業、屋台から初代・中野太一郎が銀座2丁目に開店、1999年89歳で他界。3代目和彦さん(広東料理で修業、26歳で継承)が2代目の父・喜久雄さん、母・きよ子さんと営む。2016年ビル建て替えで3年休業、2019年再開時に麺とワンタンの皮を自家製に。スープは鶏・煮干、醤油の中華そば一つ。ワンタンメン1000円(当時)、メンマは乾燥メンマを4日かけて戻す。カウンター8・テーブル4の12席。テレビ東京(2022): 昭和31年創業。食べログ: 2019年5月30日再開、現金のみ。

cultural_comfort.note: A family-run 12-seat room; staff take your order in the queue and buy the ticket for you, cash only. Many overseas visitors; short, straight noodles easy to eat for those not used to slurping.

gf_cross_contamination.text: The noodles and wonton skins are made in-house; every bowl shares the one shoyu soup.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The single soup is finished with soy sauce (醤油がまろやかにまとめたスープ); the menma and chashu are seasoned in the house style.

vegan_cross_contact.text: A chicken and niboshi soup, with pork-thigh chashu and meat-filled wontons.

tokyo_fancl_brown_rice_meals_ginza.gf_detail: [Owner review 2026-10-24: GF raised to Strong GF focus. The claim covers the menu, not the facility — check drinks (beer) and sauces.] The restaurant says every item on its menu is gluten-free, made without wheat flour (「全てのメニューは小麦粉を使用しないグルテンフリーとなっております」). The pasta is made fresh in-house each day from brown-rice flour, and the bread is a brown-rice bread. Celiac diners on FindMeGlutenFree consistently report eating there without symptoms. Two cautions. The shop's claim covers the menu, not the facility, and it does not describe how it handles cross-contact. A featured FMGF review warns that most of the menu is gluten-free 'but not absolutely everything'. Tell them you are celiac when you book: the shop asks guests with food allergies to say so at reservation. Check the drinks too, because beer is normally barley.
tokyo_fancl_brown_rice_meals_ginza.vegan_detail: The weekday lunch plate lets you choose a vegan main ('ヴィーガンメニュー') from five. The starter plate includes soy-milk whip, but the shop does not say whether its other starters are vegan. Ask for the vegan main and check the starter plate and soup.
tokyo_fancl_brown_rice_meals_ginza.hours_raw: Lunch 11:30–16:00; café 14:00–16:00; dinner 17:00–22:00 on weekdays and 17:00–21:00 on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays. Closed one day a month (check the shop notices). Weekend lunch courses need a reservation; a ¥500 table charge applies at dinner.
tokyo_fancl_brown_rice_meals_ginza.notes: [Gluten-free · brown-rice Italian] The basement restaurant of FANCL Ginza Square, the cosmetics and supplements company's ten-floor Ginza building, open since September 2019. It cooks Italian without wheat flour. The fresh pasta is made by hand every day from a blended brown-rice flour and still has an al dente bite. The bread is brown rice, the rice is FANCL's own germinated brown rice, and the dolci are gluten-free too. There are weekday lunch plates, weekend lunch courses and a build-your-own dinner. It has 36 seats, including a private room that looks onto a waterfall. It is a fixture of celiac travellers' Tokyo lists, with 130+ reviews on FindMeGlutenFree. The brown-rice bread is sold to take away.

tokyo_glutenfree_kushiage_su.gf_detail: [Owner review 2026-10-24: GF raised to Dedicated gluten-free. Still confirm the soy sauce and miso are wheat-free when you book.] The shop is a gluten-free kushiage specialist (グルテンフリー串揚げ専門店) and says it can accommodate guests with a gluten allergy or celiac disease. Celiac diners on FindMeGlutenFree describe it as completely gluten-free, report no symptoms, and mention a celiac-safe rice beer. One thing the shop does not state: it uses soy sauce, miso and other soy seasonings throughout the course, but does not say on its booking page that they are wheat-free. Message the shop by Instagram DM or email before you book to confirm, as it asks for all allergy questions.
tokyo_glutenfree_kushiage_su.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The shop says plainly that it cannot accommodate vegan requests. The omakase is built on seafood, and even the pescatarian version uses dairy and eggs.
tokyo_glutenfree_kushiage_su.hours_raw: Dinner 19:00 (one seating; the course starts when all guests have arrived), Tuesday–Sunday; Sunday lunch 12:00. Closed Mondays. Reservation only, through TableCheck, until 18:00 the day before. No children under 6.
tokyo_glutenfree_kushiage_su.notes: [Gluten-free · Mom & Pop · kushiage omakase] A six-seat, reservation-only counter where a single chef cooks and serves a seasonal omakase of gluten-free fried skewers: two starters, eleven skewers, soup, a palate cleanser and dessert. Everyone starts together at 7 p.m. There is no sign. You walk through the Ginza Park Building and buzz 201 at the side entrance. Celiac reviewers call it the best gluten-free meal they have had in Tokyo, with mentions of the chef's warmth and a gluten-free rice beer. The course is seafood-heavy and soy-seasoned, so it suits neither vegans nor guests with a soy allergy.

tokyo_ain_soph_ginza.gf_detail: Many dishes are marked 【GF】 on the shop's own menu: the signature rice-flour pancakes (fermented overnight with coconut oil), the Fukurokuju bento, green curry, the vegan pudding and most desserts. Some dishes are not tagged GF: the hummus (served with a baguette), the vegan cutlets and cutlet plate, the tomato-sauce veg-hamburg, the house ice cream and the beers (Heartland and the beer cocktails are barley). The shop notes that its factory and shop also handle other allergens and asks guests with allergies to speak to staff. This is a shared kitchen: order only the 【GF】-marked dishes and confirm.
tokyo_ain_soph_ginza.vegan_detail: Everything is 100% vegan (「全品100%ヴィーガン」): no meat, fish, dairy or eggs, only plant ingredients. Many dishes can also be made without the five pungent vegetables (素食 / oriental vegan) on request.
tokyo_ain_soph_ginza.hours_raw: Restaurant (2F–4F): weekdays lunch 11:30–16:00 (L.O. 15:00) and dinner 17:00–21:00 (L.O. 20:00); weekends add breakfast 8:00–11:30. Patisserie (1F): 11:30–20:30. Hours change at times — the shop points to its Instagram.
tokyo_ain_soph_ginza.notes: [Vegan · GF options] The flagship of AIN SOPH., a Tokyo vegan group that opened here in December 2009 and has since added Shinjuku, Ikebukuro and Kyoto. A vegan patisserie fills the ground floor, with the pudding, raisin-butter sandwiches and cookies. Three floors of restaurant sit above. The draw is the 'heavenly' vegan pancake, made from Kyushu rice flour and coconut oil, fermented overnight and tagged gluten-free. The Ginza-only Fukurokuju bento is a tiered box (お重) of salads, bagna cauda, tofu Spanish omelette, soy-meat kara-age, organic brown rice and spinach green curry. Organic wine and craft beer are served. Weekend breakfast starts at 8:00. Many dishes can be made without garlic, onion and leek.

roles: vegan restaurant group (AIN SOPH.) — flagship
chef_bio.background: AIN SOPH. began at this Ginza shop in 2009 and runs sister restaurants in Shinjuku (Journey), Ikebukuro (Soar) and Kyoto (Journey Kyoto). The founder's statement on the shop page says the idea came at a turning point in life, from a bowl of tea at a tea ceremony that felt like the power of nature in a single drop.
chef_bio.philosophy: 'Our cuisine is a meal for us to return to our origin.'
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour vegan pancakes; Fukurokuju bento; vegan patisserie (pudding, raisin sandwiches).

tokyo_ginza_manpuku.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. A neighbourhood Chinese diner (machi-chūka). The chuka soba is thin curly wheat noodles in a soy-sauce soup, and its tare is the soy-based chashu sauce. The rest of the menu is fried rice, gyoza and stir-fries from one wok kitchen. No gluten-free dish is mentioned in any source.
tokyo_ginza_manpuku.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The soup combines seafood and meat stocks, the chashu is soy-braised pork thigh, and the signature pork rice is fried with chopped chashu. No vegetarian dish is mentioned.
tokyo_ginza_manpuku.hours_raw: Mon 11:00–14:30 & 17:00–22:00; Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat 11:00–15:00 & 17:00–22:00; Fri 11:30–15:00 & 17:00–22:00; closed Sundays and holidays. Cash only. Reservations for banquets only.
tokyo_ginza_manpuku.notes: [Mom & Pop · since the 1920s] Manpuku began as a chuka-soba street stall in the Taishō era. In 1929 the founder opened a shop in old Kobikichō, close to Kabuki-za. He had trained in Western cooking, so it ran as a 'Western and Chinese' (西支料理) restaurant; the faded wooden sign by the door still says so. His grandson Kubo Hidetaka is the third owner and has turned the menu towards Chinese food. Pork rice is the one Western dish left: ketchup fried rice made with the house chashu instead of chicken. The chuka soba keeps the soup the earlier generations made: a soy soup of seafood and meat stocks with a hint of ginger and negi oil, thin curly noodles, and a triangle of thin omelette on top. The wooden building was rebuilt in 2003 but kept its old frontage, and some families have been coming for four generations. Cash only.

roles: third-generation owner
chef_bio.origin: Born and raised in Ginza; the shop founded as a Taishō-era stall, in Kobikichō since 1929
chef_bio.background: Kubo's grandfather, the founder, worked from early morning till night; the family lived simply in the stall years. Kubo gave up a university-era dream after an injury, trained in other Chinese restaurants at his father's insistence, and took over from his father at about 25. Under him the Western dishes (omurice, cutlets) gave way to more Chinese ones, such as liver and chives and ebi-tama.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「先代からスープの味を変えてない」 — the soup has not changed since the previous generations.
chef_bio.specialty: Chuka soba with a triangle omelette; pork rice (ketchup fried rice with chashu); set meals.

anecdotes.text: It ran as a 西支料理 (Western-and-Chinese) restaurant, because the founder came from Western cooking; the old wooden sign by the door still faintly reads 「西支料理」.
Pork rice, the last Western dish, uses the house chashu rather than chicken or bacon: 「うちは西支料理なので、鶏肉やベーコンを入れないんです」.
The tare is the chashu braising sauce; the soup recipe is secret.
The shop is among 28 Ginza institutions that made collaboration T-shirts with Uniqlo; Manpuku's carries its chuka soba.
「今や、家族４代でお見えになるお客さまもいらっしゃいます」 — some families now come four generations deep.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: さんたつ(2023.10.25): 大正時代に屋台から、昭和4年(1929)に旧木挽町に店舗。初代は洋食出身で西支料理店。3代目・久保英恭さん(祖父が初代、25歳頃に父から継承)。2003年改築。中華そば800円・ポークライス950円(当時)。醤油スープは魚介と動物系、ショウガ、ネギ油、細めのちぢれ麺、豚モモのチャーシュー、メンマ・ほうれん草・ナルト・三角の薄焼き卵。現代ビジネス: 屋台時代から約100年変わらぬ中華そば。食べログ: 27席、現金のみ、日祝休。

cultural_comfort.note: A retro brick-fronted diner with counter and tables; cash only. Families and regulars; reservations only for banquets.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Thin curly ramen noodles; fried rice, gyoza and stir-fries come from the same wok kitchen.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The tare for the chuka soba is the chashu braising sauce, and the chashu is braised in soy sauce (しっかりと醤油で煮込まれて).

vegan_cross_contact.text: The soup combines seafood and meat stocks (魚介と動物系); pork rice is fried with chopped chashu.

tokyo_ginza_funamizaka.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The noodles are made to an early-Shōwa recipe from coarse-ground wheat flour, and the chashu is braised in soy sauce and mirin. Gyoza and a soy-sauce ramen are also on the menu. No gluten-free noodle is mentioned.
tokyo_ginza_funamizaka.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The clear soup is simmered from kombu, dried scallop, chicken frames, pork bones and vegetables, and every bowl carries pork-belly chashu.
tokyo_ginza_funamizaka.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–04:00 (last order 03:30); Sun & holidays 11:00–22:00. Cards and IC payments accepted.
tokyo_ginza_funamizaka.notes: [Mom & Pop · Hakodate shio] A Hakodate ramen shop near Kabuki-za, open since 2001 under the banner 'early-Shōwa Hakodate ramen'. Its founder had been won over by ramen on a trip to Hakodate. The present owner, Kiribayashi Masahiko, once cooked at a well-known Chinese restaurant and worked here in 2010–12. He left to run his own shop, and when that site was cleared in 2014 he took this one over; regulars greeted him with 'welcome back'. The bowl to order is shio soba. It is a golden, clear soup of Hokkaido ma-kombu, dried scallop, chicken frames, pork bone and vegetables, seasoned with Bizen rock salt. The noodles are rebuilt from an early-Shōwa recipe with coarse wheat flour and coloured with gardenia, because the old recipe comes out grey. The chashu sits in a soy-and-mirin tare that has been topped up for years. The room is fitted out like a Hokkaido fishing-port shack, and it is open until 4 a.m.

roles: owner (since 2014)
chef_bio.origin: Shop founded 2001 by its first owner; Ginza 2-chōme
chef_bio.background: Kiribayashi came to cooking through a student job in a ramen shop and later cooked at a well-known Chinese restaurant, but preferred ramen because 'you see the customer's reaction in front of you'. He worked at Funamizaka from 2010, went independent in 2012, and took over this shop in 2014 when his own was cleared for redevelopment.
chef_bio.philosophy: He keeps the founder's 'early-Shōwa Hakodate ramen' as the base and adjusts it to the times. The shio soba's stock proportions now make it a little richer, because customers prefer richer bowls.
chef_bio.specialty: Shio soba (Bizen rock salt, kombu–scallop–chicken–pork clear soup); early-Shōwa-recipe noodles; long-topped-up chashu tare.

anecdotes.text: 「再オープンすると、知った顔がたくさんお見えになって『おかえり』って言われました」 — on reopening in 2014, many familiar faces came in and said 'welcome back'.
The noodles follow an early-Shōwa recipe with coarse-ground flour; made that way they come out grey, so they are coloured with gardenia (クチナシ).
The salt is Bizen rock salt, chosen by the founder for its plain, old-fashioned taste.
The chashu tare has been topped up continuously — 「時間と共に仕上がっている最高の調味料」.

tokyo_yurakucho_tani_ramen.notes: [Mom & Pop · under the tracks] A small weekday-only ramen shop under the JR viaduct opposite Tokyo International Forum. An 18-time regular dates it to the late 1960s. The soup is a clear, golden pork-bone and chicken stock with soy sauce, which diners call rich in collagen umami yet clean. The noodles come from Maruyama Seimen, and the chashu is pork leg. The usual order is ramen with half fried rice, or wonton-men. You buy a ticket from the machine outside, which will not take the new banknotes, so the owner changes them for you inside. It has 12 seats, including a small tatami area at lunch. Cash only, and closed at weekends.

chef_bio.origin: Under the JR tracks, Marunouchi 3-chōme; dated by a long-time regular to 1967–68
chef_bio.background: A long-running owner-run ramen shop. No owner name or founding story appears in any source found; the founding date comes from a regular's review (which gives both 1967 and 1968).

Miso and shoyu butter ramen cost the same with or without butter. A curry ramen is built on the ramen broth. There are drinks and snacks for a late crowd. Smoking is allowed throughout, and payment is cash only.

tokyo_ginza_bonten.notes: [Ramen · tsukesoba] A 20-seat shop opened in 2011, decorated like an old farmhouse with beams and handwritten menus on the walls. The president chose the décor and the name; the manager, Satō Hikaru, says the name was probably picked because the characters look cool. The draw is 麻辛丸, read 'machine gun', a registered trademark. Extra-thick, chewy noodles that taste of wheat go into a red, sour-hot dip on a chicken-frame base, with shredded chashu and house menma. Pork-loin chashu is the top topping. There is also a very light Japanese-style ramen on ultra-thin noodles. Office workers come at lunch, hotel guests in the afternoon and drinkers late at night. There is an English and Korean menu. Cash only.

company-run (a 社長 owns the shop)

Lunch is local office workers, afternoons are tourists checking into hotels, and nights are drinkers after a last bowl.

tokyo_ginza_ramen_ichiro.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. Wheat noodles: curly medium-thick for shoyu, shio and curry, thin straight from Sugano Seimen for the clam ramen. The tare includes soy sauce, and the clam version uses shottsuru fish sauce. No gluten-free option is mentioned.
tokyo_ginza_ramen_ichiro.vegan_detail: Not vegan. Every bowl uses the same soup of Aomori Shamorock chicken with grilled flying fish (yaki-ago) and tomato. The clam ramen adds Jūsan-ko clams, and all bowls carry large pork chashu.
tokyo_ginza_ramen_ichiro.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–23:00 (last order 22:30); Sat, Sun & holidays 11:00–21:00. No fixed holiday; may close early when soup runs out. Cards and QR payments accepted.
tokyo_ginza_ramen_ichiro.notes: [Mom & Pop · Aomori ramen] A six-seat basement counter under a red lantern, 30 seconds from Ginza Station. Owner Hasegawa Ichirō, whose name is on the door, had run soba and Italian restaurants and lived in the US for about five years. He opened here in December 2016, choosing Ginza with an eye to opening abroad. Several people around the shop were from Aomori, so he built the ramen on Aomori produce: Shamorock chicken, and clams from Lake Jūsan, billed as 'Japan's best'. Every bowl shares one soup of Shamorock chicken, grilled flying fish and tomato, now cooked between clear and cloudy. The clam ramen's tare adds shottsuru fish sauce. Pork chashu comes in very large slices. In 2026 he still cooks almost single-handed, and the shop had not raised its prices since opening as of 2023.

roles: owner-chef
chef_bio.background: Hasegawa ran soba restaurants, Italian places and other businesses before a friendship with a ramen craftsman led him to open a ramen shop. He studied in the US and lived there about five years, and picked Ginza with overseas expansion in mind; COVID changed that, and he kept the shop open every day to survive.
chef_bio.philosophy: Keep refining the bowl and keep prices easy for customers.
chef_bio.specialty: Shijimi (Jūsan-ko clam) ramen; Aomori Shamorock chicken soup; curry ramen; nebuta-zuke rice.

anecdotes.text: 「たまたま店の関係者に青森出身者が何人かいたから、青森の食材を使ったラーメンにしようってことになったんです」.
The soup was once a clear chintan; he turned up the heat to draw more from the chicken, and now calls it 'between paitan and chintan'. Tomato was added to the stock.
Grilled sardines (iwashi yaki-boshi) became unobtainable during COVID, so grilled flying fish (yaki-ago) replaced them.
A cut-out of the baseball player Ichirō stands in the corner. Asked whether he is aiming to be the Ichirō of ramen: 「なれるといいんですけど」.
October 2026: "The skill of a one-man operation in Ginza is remarkable" — the clam ramen arrived in under five minutes.

tokyo_ginza_genraku.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. Five kinds of wheat noodle are matched to the bowls. The house 元らーめん is a shoyu ramen, and the chashu is simmered in the shop's own tare. No gluten-free noodle is mentioned.
tokyo_ginza_genraku.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The soup is pork knuckle bones simmered for three days with vegetables and chicken frames, under a thick layer of pork back fat, with pork-belly chashu.
tokyo_ginza_genraku.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 11:00–23:00; Wed 11:00–22:30; Sat, Sun & holidays 11:00–20:00. Open daily except some days over Golden Week, Obon and New Year.
tokyo_ginza_genraku.notes: [Ramen · back-fat tonkotsu] The Ginza branch of らーめん元楽, a back-fat ramen company whose head shop opened in Kuramae in 1995 and which also has a shop in Shimbashi. The soup uses only pork knuckle bones (genkotsu), simmered for three days with vegetables and chicken frames, skimmed hard, until it turns mellow and jellies when cold. The back fat that covers the bowl is fried, blanched, washed and simmered in the soup for two hours, so it comes out sweet and fluffy rather than greasy. Order 元 for shoyu or 楽 for shio. The pork-belly chashu is braised two and a half hours until it cuts with chopsticks. Half buta-meshi (pork over rice) is the usual side. Garlic and doubanjiang are on the counter.

roles: ramen company (Genraku Co., Ltd.) — Ginza branch
chef_bio.origin: Founded 1995 (company profile); shops in Kuramae, Ginza and Shimbashi
chef_bio.background: Run by Genraku Co., Ltd., which operates the Kuramae head shop, this Ginza branch and a Shimbashi branch, and sells its chashu online.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「徹底的にクセ・臭いを抜いた背脂」 — back fat with every trace of animal smell removed.
chef_bio.specialty: Back-fat shoyu (元) and shio (楽) ramen on a three-day genkotsu soup; tender pork-belly chashu; buta-meshi.

anecdotes.text: The pork soup uses only the femur ("genkotsu"), rich in cartilage and collagen, simmered three days with vegetables and chicken frames until it sets like jelly.
The back fat is fried, blanched, hand-washed of excess fat and scum, then simmered two hours in the pork soup.
Five noodles for five styles, from ultra-thin for cold noodles to thick for tsukemen and abura-soba; curly thin noodles for the standard 元 and 楽 ramen.

The niku-soba piles on chashu. Ginza also serves the uncle's Hinai-jidori chicken soba, which a 2026 diner says the Ōji branch doesn't have, and a niboshi tsukemen whose noodles come soaked in a kombu-water-like broth. 12 seats.

tokyo_soranoiro_ginza.notes: [Ramen · vegan & GF options] The flagship of Soranoiro, the ramen company that opened in Kōjimachi just after the 2011 earthquake. The chuka soba here is built on the frames of Amakusa Daiō, one of Japan's largest native chickens, with niboshi, bonito and aromatic vegetables. Its noodles are made of domestic wheat at the company's Kōjimachi workshop, and the chashu is Seto mochi-buta pork from Fukuyama in three cuts. Celiac and vegan travellers on FindMeGlutenFree report a separate gluten-free menu and a vegan gluten-free ramen at this shop.

tokyo_mendokoro_ginzasa.notes: [Mom & Pop · dashi ramen] A dark, quiet shop in a back alley between Ginza and Shimbashi, opened in 2010 by Sasanuma Takahiro after 18 years as a Japanese-cuisine chef. He worked at a Ginza restaurant known for sea-bream chazuke, and built his shop around the same idea: eat the ramen, eat some sea-bream rice plain, then pour the soup over the rest to make chazuke. The soup is chicken and pork stock, chilled overnight and stripped of fat, then joined with kombu and niboshi dashi; it is not a sea-bream broth, as many first-timers assume. Choose salt or white soy sauce. The bowl, modelled on a kaiseki soup course, carries pink sea-bream fish balls and pork-belly chashu torched to order. The spouted bowls were made by his pottery teacher in Hannō-yaki, so the soup pours neatly onto the rice. Listed in the Tabelog Ramen TOKYO 100 every year from 2017 to 2025. Queues form at the 11:15 opening.

tokyo_ginza_soryu.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. Every bowl is wheat noodles, including whole-wheat flat noodles for the tsukemen. The tare are soy-sauce based: Kikkogo shoyu, white soy sauce and shiro-tamari, or a shoyu tonkotsu. No gluten-free option is mentioned.

tokyo_ginza_soryu.notes: [Ramen · Tokyo shoyu, late night] The Ginza shop of 株式会社創龍, the company behind the Nogata Hope ramen shops (its first Nogata Hope opened in 1988). Opened in October 2018 as a step-up, glass-fronted room with high ceilings, sofa seats and a counter facing the kitchen. The focus is Tokyo: Kikkogo soy sauce from Kondō Jōzō, which the shop calls Tokyo's only soy-sauce brewery, and Edo-na greens. The signature 大江戸焦がし醤油 burns the house shoyu tare in lard, and the burnt lard seals the clear soup so it stays hot. Other bowls: a mellow white shoyu with shiro-tamari, ishiru and Izu Ōshima salt; a black shoyu with flying-fish dashi; Nogata Hope's original tonkotsu shoyu 元; the richer 濃 with fish dashi, garlic oil and spicy miso; and a tomato ramen. Open until 3 a.m. six nights a week, it fills with after-drinks crowds.

tokyo_ginza_tsukiya.notes: [Ramen · clear tonkotsu] A Ginza-only spin-off of the Hakata shop 豚そば月や, opened on the sixth floor of GINZA SIX in April 2023. It rebuilt its Hakata pork soba from the ingredients up into a clear tonkotsu, light enough that diners finish the broth, with thin noodles ordered by firmness, from firm to extra firm. The bowl comes with a suggested order of add-ins: green onion, nori, chashu, a squeeze of kabosu, then pickled ginger. The other draw is Hakata tarako rice with a special spicy sauce; the cod roe comes from Yamato Violets of the Fukuya group, under a supply contract renewed in April 2026. There are dishes brought in from Fukuoka restaurants too, and a ¥3,300 Tsukiya set adds shumai, fried horse mackerel and tomato. Queues, many of them overseas visitors, form at lunch.

tokyo_chuka_santomi.notes: [Mom & Pop · machi-chūka since 1971] A rare independent neighbourhood Chinese restaurant in Marunouchi, under the brick railway arches near Tokyo Station's south exit, where the yellow Hato buses line up. The owner's uncle opened it in 1971. Owner Hirata Kōichi worked here for about forty years and took over as the second generation around 2014. Chefs with twenty or thirty years in the kitchen still cook the founder's recipes, and the menu has barely changed. It runs to more than sixty dishes, more than twenty of them noodles. The owner's recommendations are the tanmen and the meat-and-vegetable stir-fry, the most popular dish, which becomes a set for ¥200 more. Regulars also come for liver with garlic chives, offal stamina ramen and miso ramen. Prices are low for Marunouchi: ramen was ¥800 in September 2026. You pay first for a coloured plastic meal ticket, and Marunouchi office workers queue even after lunch.

tokyo_haruchan_ramen_shimbashi.notes: [Ramen · the Haru-chan original] The first shop of はるちゃんラーメン: six counter seats on the ground floor of the old Shimbashi Ekimae Building, opened in August 2021 by a woman who goes by Haru-chan and had worked in ramen shops for about twenty years. In 2022 she ran it single-handed in a kitchen barely big enough to turn round in, styled like 'Haru-chan's kitchen at home' in warm wood. She calls it chuka soba, not ramen, because chuka soba sounds warmer. The soup is a light salt base: the pork stock from braising the chashu, with niboshi and aromatic vegetables. It is filled to the brim so it stays hot to the end. Flat Daruma Seimen noodles, two cuts of chashu (shoulder and belly) sliced only to order, and pastel fu on top for colour. 2026 diners describe it as a Michelin Bib Gourmand shop, with a queue around noon. The brand opened a second shop in Ginza 3-chōme in 2024.

tokyo_menya_hyottoko.notes: [Ramen · yuzu wafu shio] A seven-seat counter in the basement of the Tokyo Kōtsū Kaikan by Yūrakuchō Station, on the narrow 'Yokotcho' passage. It opened in 2005 as the sister shop of the long-running sweets house 甘味おかめ in the same building, and the company that runs Okame, Ishizuka Kōsan, runs it too. The menu is four bowls: wafu ramen and wafu chashu-men, each also made with yuzu. The soup is a pale-gold clear stock of chicken bones with bonito and kombu, very light. The yuzu versions get freshly grated yuzu in the centre to stir in, with mitsuba, mizuna, menma and negi. Thin noodles, three large smoky slices of chashu on the chashu bowls, and Okame's chameshi (tea-flavoured rice) on the side. Bowls arrive in about three minutes, and the queue moves fast; buy your ticket from the machine before joining it. It was ¥780 for wafu ramen in May 2026.

tokyo_mago_rinsha.notes: [Tsukemen · Rokurinsha group] A 16-seat counter under the railway arches near the Hato Bus terminal at Tokyo Station, opened in January 2020 by 松富士食品, the company behind Rokurinsha and Sharin. On weekdays it opens at 7 a.m. with a ¥600 morning ramen (to 10:30): thin straight noodles, lots of ginger, a lighter broth with gentle niboshi and chashu scraps, and extra noodles instead of a large size. From late morning it is tsukemen: thick, chewy noodles served cold, a dipping soup one 2026 diner found meat-led rather than seafood-led, grated garlic to add, and portions so big that a 'large' surprised two reviewers. Spicy and chilled mala tsukemen, cold sesame noodles, chicken-oil rice and egg on rice are on the menu. Buy a ticket inside, wait, and collect your bowl when your number is called.

tokyo_oshima_ramen_ginza.notes: [Ramen · late night, Shōwa retro] A long-running counter in Ginza 8-chōme with an open kitchen, where Ginza drinkers end the night: weekdays it is open until 3:30 a.m. A diner returning after twenty years in 2026 found the room unchanged. Regulars order the miso ramen: medium-thick straight noodles, bean sprouts, corn, menma, chashu and egg, made punchier with the 'oni' spicy miso. Others come for the Oshima gyoza, eaten with grated daikon and hot mustard, and fried rice, which is also sold to take away. Lunch sets were about ¥1,000–1,100 in 2026, with a complimentary dish of boiled bean sprouts. Tabelog links it to apraise.co.jp, whose Oshima page is gone, so the operator is not established.

tokyo_blood_moon_shimbashi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The noodles are wheat, including whole-wheat thin and medium-thick noodles made with Kanno Seimen. The meat miso is seasoned with Chinese soy sauce, the jarichi pork cutlet is fried in a soy-ginger marinade, and there is a soy-sauce chuka soba. No gluten-free option is mentioned.
tokyo_blood_moon_shimbashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The tantan soup is built on chicken and dried ingredients with shijimi clams, kombu and shiitake, under a sesame-cashew paste, and is topped with minced domestic pork. The night-only bowl adds a large fried chicken cutlet.
tokyo_blood_moon_shimbashi.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–16:00 and 17:00–23:30 (L.O. 23:00); Sat 11:30–15:00; closed Sundays (Tabelog). Cash only; the ticket machine took only older banknotes in 2026.
tokyo_blood_moon_shimbashi.notes: [Mom & Pop · tantanmen and a bar] Takanashi Tomoyoshi grew up in Shimbashi, worked as a bartender in Ginza, and in 2021 opened this 'neo ramen' shop in his home neighbourhood, because he liked the idea of ramen with drinks. Eight counter seats downstairs and a Chinese dining bar upstairs, marked by a tantanmen lantern next to the Daiwa Roynet Hotel. He asked an old friend, the owner of the Kinshichō tantanmen shop noodle house 錦鯉, to produce a tantanmen that goes with alcohol. It is built on a house paste of freshly ground sesame and cashew, a soup of chicken, dried ingredients, shijimi clams, Hokkaidō kombu and shiitake, minced domestic pork, and a chilli oil of four chillies. Noodles were developed with Kanno Seimen, with whole wheat in them. There is also a dry tantanmen with hand-massaged medium-thick noodles, a tantan tsukemen with black vinegar, a shoyu chuka soba, and a night-only 'Tōgenkyō' tantanmen with a fried chicken cutlet. Spice and numbness levels are adjustable. Try the ¥300 jarichi, a ginger-soy pork cutlet, dropped into the soup like pāko-men.

tokyo_shimbashi_new_tomochin.notes: [Ramen · standing counter] The fourth shop of Kōenji's Tomochin Ramen (Tabelog), opened September 2023 in the basement of the Shimbashi Ekimae Building, and a famous morning-to-afternoon queue. Six standing places at the counter, one dish: chuka soba for ¥850, with wakame for ¥100 and free, refillable rice; hand over the yellow rice ticket with your ramen ticket. The soup is a clear soy colour with a thin layer of pork fat, light but meaty, and regulars add wakame and soften the green onions in the hot oil. 2026 diners were split between those who call it the pinnacle of morning ramen and those who found it mild.

tokyo_odo_no_shirushi_shimbashi.notes: [Ramen · iekei, Ōdōya group] A 15-seat Shimbashi shop of 王道乃印, a brand of the Ōdōya iekei group (other 王道乃印 shops include Kashiwa and, from 24 October 2026, Ōta in Gunma; a 2026 diner also mentions Akihabara). Opened May 2025. The bowl is a rich, marrow-heavy pork-bone soup with a sharp tare, medium-thick noodles, smoky rare chashu, nori and spinach; noodle firmness, richness and oil are set to taste. Grated garlic and ginger are free on the table. Ramen ¥950 and rice ¥150 in October 2026. Open until 4 a.m. on weekdays. A regular in 2026 found it less busy than before and the noodles changed; another called it a lighter Ōdōya.

roles: shop of the 王道家 group brand 王道乃印
chef_bio.background: 王道乃印 is a brand within the 王道家 (Ōdōya) iekei group; group shops train new owners in the group kitchens (PR TIMES, 2026). No source names this shop's operator.
chef_bio.specialty: Ōdōya-style iekei; special ramen with three slices of chashu, nori and spinach.

anecdotes.text: "A lighter version of Oudouya. It's smoother than the original, yet it captures the richness of the meat flavor, the sharpness of the tare… However, it does leave you extremely thirsty."
A diner expecting three slices of chashu got four: "I must have used up my luck on something trivial."

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: PR TIMES(2026年): 「王道乃印 野上家」は王道家系列として群馬県太田市に2026年10月24日オープン、王道乃印 柏店で研修、ラーメン950円・王道乃印ラーメン1,450円。食べログ: 王道乃印 新橋、2025年5月7日オープン、平日11:00〜翌4:00、土日祝11:00〜22:00、15席、現金のみ。2026年の口コミ: ラーメン950円・ライス150円、特製+半ライス1,550円、白髪ねぎラーメン海苔増し1,300円、燻製香のレアチャーシュー、にんにく・生姜は卓上で無料。

cultural_comfort.note: Ticket machine (cash only); preferences for firmness, richness and oil. Self-serve water and paper aprons; compact seating.

tokyo_tenhou_shimbashi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. Wakayama-style chuka soba on thin wheat noodles, tsukemen, shumai and karaage. No gluten-free option is mentioned.
tokyo_tenhou_shimbashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The chuka soba carries plenty of chashu, the tsukemen dip is described as strongly animal-based, and the sets add shumai and karaage.

tokyo_tenhou_shimbashi.notes: [Ramen · Wakayama chuka soba] A Shimbashi branch of 天鳳, a brand of Fujio Food System, selling Wakayama-style chuka soba under that name on the sign. The bowl looks rich, with thin noodles and plenty of chashu; diners in 2026 disagreed on whether it was light or heavy. The tsukemen (¥920 in October 2026) has medium-thick straight noodles, three thick slices of pork belly and cubed grilled chashu. Sets pair the ramen with shumai, rice and karaage. Quiet in the afternoon, with regulars on a daytime chūhai.

roles: brand of 株式会社フジオフードシステム
chef_bio.background: Listed on the Fujio Food System site as 天鳳 新橋店.
chef_bio.specialty: Wakayama chuka soba; tsukemen with pork belly; A/C sets with shumai and karaage.

anecdotes.text: An October 2026 diner who ate Wakayama chuka soba daily on a business trip 40 years ago came in on the strength of the sign alone.
"The manager seemed to be from Wakayama, as he spoke in a Kansai dialect."

tokyo_kaidashi_ramen_shirahara.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. One ramen on wheat noodles, sold alone or as a set with five pieces of red-vinegar sushi served with soy sauce. No gluten-free option is mentioned.
tokyo_kaidashi_ramen_shirahara.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The soup is a shellfish broth, finished by steeping a basket of bonito flakes in it, and the set adds fish sushi.
tokyo_kaidashi_ramen_shirahara.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:30–14:00 (lunch only); closed Sundays (Tabelog). PayPay accepted; no cards.
tokyo_kaidashi_ramen_shirahara.notes: [Ramen · shellfish broth, lunch only] By night this space in the Shimbashi Ekimae Building is a shellfish-and-sashimi izakaya; at lunch it turns into a ramen counter with one bowl. The soup is a shellfish (kai-dashi) broth, and each bowl comes with a little basket of bonito flakes: dip it for about ten seconds, then lift it out. Order it alone or in a ¥1,500 set with five pieces of sushi on red-vinegar rice. Diners call the soup light and refreshing but full of flavour, and the turnover is quick because there is so little to choose from.

chef_bio.origin: Shimbashi Ekimae Bldg No. 1; opening year not found
chef_bio.background: A June 2026 diner says the izakaya 「貝出汁 刺身専門店 しらはら」 serves shellfish and sashimi at night and becomes 「貝出汁らぁ麺 しらはら」 by day. No source names the owner or company.

A diner on a typhoon day was the only customer at 1:15 p.m. — and still could not decide whether ramen and sushi belong together.

tokyo_uogashiya_shimbashi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The ramen is medium-thick curly wheat noodles in a salty bonito broth. The sushi is nigiri on red-vinegar rice; no source says whether it is served with soy sauce or what that is made from. No gluten-free option is mentioned.
tokyo_uogashiya_shimbashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The ramen is a bonito (katsuo) broth finished with more bonito flakes, topped with chashu, and the other half of the menu is fish sushi.
tokyo_uogashiya_shimbashi.hours_raw: Daily 07:00–05:00 (next morning); closed 1–3 January (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted. Ticket machine outside.
tokyo_uogashiya_shimbashi.notes: [Ramen + sushi · nearly 24 hours] The Shimbashi branch, opened August 2024, of a sushi-and-ramen chain whose head shop is in Yokohama's central wholesale market. It now has shops in Shibuya, Noge, Tsuruyachō and Minato Mirai, and is selling franchises. The fish comes straight from Toyosu and the Yokohama market, and the nigiri is on red-vinegar rice. The ramen is 追いかつお: a salty bonito broth with medium-thick curly noodles, two slices of chashu, nori, menma, radish sprouts and negi. A tea strainer of bonito flakes, shaved in the shop, is stirred in for about ten seconds. The ramen-and-five-nigiri set was ¥1,500 in October 2026, and the ramen alone ¥890. Ten counter seats; buy a ticket outside; open from 7 a.m. to 5 a.m.

roles: sushi-and-ramen chain (head shop at Yokohama Central Wholesale Market; franchising)
chef_bio.background: The brand lists shops in Shimbashi and Shibuya (Tokyo) and its head shop at the Yokohama Central Wholesale Market, plus Noge, Tsuruyachō, Minato Mirai and Yokohama Landmark. It advertises franchises on its site.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「豊洲市場・横浜市中央卸売市場より直接仕入れ」 — fish bought directly from the Toyosu and Yokohama wholesale markets.
chef_bio.specialty: Oi-katsuo ramen with five-piece nigiri sets; bluefin tuna nigiri.

anecdotes.text: The brand gives away one chūtoro nigiri on the 10th of every month (shop Instagram feed on its site).
"As soon as I walked in, I was greeted by the wonderful aroma of bonito flakes, which they seemed to be shaving right there in the restaurant."
October 2026: "Inside the tea strainer, there are bonito flakes, which you mix for about 10 seconds to enhance the broth's flavor" — Oikatsuo ramen ¥890.

tokyo_menya_nobunaga_kyobashi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. Every bowl uses the house curly wheat noodles in a rich seafood-and-chicken paitan. Fried karaage and abura-soba are also on the menu. Tabelog notes that allergy information is available, so ask the staff, but no gluten-free noodle is mentioned.
tokyo_menya_nobunaga_kyobashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The soup is chicken paitan with seafood, simmered for 48 hours, and is finished with seafood powder and shrimp oil. The bowls carry chicken chashu, and a wagyu-and-truffle ramen is on the menu.
tokyo_menya_nobunaga_kyobashi.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–03:00 (next day); closing days may vary (Tabelog). All cards, IC, e-money and QR accepted.
tokyo_menya_nobunaga_kyobashi.notes: [Ramen · seafood chicken paitan, late night] The first shop, opened December 2024, of 麺屋NOBUNAGA, which now has four: Kyōbashi, Kayabachō, Shintomichō and a Tsukiji flagship, 'SHOGUN', that also serves tempura courses. The bowl is a 48-hour seafood chicken paitan, milky white turning golden, with the company's own curly noodles and chicken chashu. The all-toppings bowl adds egg, nori, seafood powder, shrimp oil, crisp onion and mizuna; a squeeze of lemon cuts the richness. Tsukemen are served at Kyōbashi, Kayabachō and Shintomichō only. Open from 10 a.m. to 3 a.m., it fills late at night, much of the crowd from overseas. Founder Usuda Noriyasu is a former Maritime Self-Defense Force sailor who became an izakaya-industry manager and trainer.

chef_bio.chef_name: 薄田典靖 (Usuda Noriyasu, founder and CEO of 株式会社NOBUNAGA)
roles: founder / company representative — not the cook at this shop
chef_bio.origin: Kyōbashi, first shop, December 2024; four shops by March 2026
chef_bio.background: Born in Saga in 1987, Usuda served in the Maritime Self-Defense Force, including a 2008 Indian Ocean deployment, then joined the izakaya company Teppen, where he became a store manager and company president. He founded DLE Holdings in 2016 and runs restaurants, salons and corporate training.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「世界に感動の一杯を届ける」 — to deliver a moving bowl to the world, with seafood chicken paitan as the house genre.
chef_bio.specialty: NOBUNAGA all-toppings ramen; 48-hour seafood chicken paitan; spicy-miso limited editions.

anecdotes.text: The menu calls the all-toppings bowl more than ten elements: chicken chashu, house egg, nori, and 「隠し味として散りばめられた魚介の粉末や海老から抽出した油」.
An October 2026 diner at 10:30 p.m. found every seat taken; "very popular among international visitors."
Another found the all-toppings tsukemen satisfying at first, but "towards the end, the greasiness became a bit overwhelming."

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式(ramen-nobunaga.com): 濃厚魚介鶏白湯、独自製法で48時間煮込んだスープ、オリジナルのちぢれ麺、鶏チャーシュー、自家製の卵、魚介の粉末、海老油など10種類以上の具材。つけ麺は京橋店・茅場町店・新富町限定。築地店SHOGUNは天麩羅お任せコース。代表取締役・薄田典靖(1987年佐賀生まれ、海上自衛隊、株式会社てっぺん、DLEホールディングス設立)。さんたつ掲載リリース: 運営 株式会社NOBUNAGA、2024年12月京橋で1号店。2026年3月新富町に4号店。食べログ: 毎日10:00〜翌3:00、20席、各種決済可、アレルギー表示あり。口コミ: 全部乗せ1,580〜1,650円、味玉ラーメン1,150円。

tokyo_iekei_kounoya_ginza.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. Iekei ramen: curly wheat noodles in a pork-bone soy-sauce soup with chicken oil. No gluten-free option is mentioned.
tokyo_iekei_kounoya_ginza.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The soup is a dark-brown pork-bone stock in the style of Budōka, made rounder with chicken oil, and the bowls carry thick chashu.
tokyo_iekei_kounoya_ginza.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–21:30; Sun 11:00–18:00 (Tabelog). Cash only; ticket machine.
tokyo_iekei_kounoya_ginza.notes: [Ramen · iekei, Budōka line] Opened 10 June 2026 by Kōno Jōji, 'George' to regulars, who spent a decade as manager of the Kichijōji shop of Budōka, the Tokyo iekei shop people travel from other prefectures for. His soup is Budōka's dark, deep pork-bone stock, of which the press release says 300 kg of bones go into a pot boiled hard, rounded off with chicken oil. Order noodle firmness, richness and oil at the counter. Ramen is ¥900 and rice ¥100, cheap for Ginza; soak the nori in the soup and wrap the rice in it. He wants to build 'a Ginza ordinary people can use every day'. The shop opened under the 'trust' scheme of Mujaki Foods, a restaurant-support company that pays the opening costs, so it is company-backed rather than independently owned. Sixteen L-shaped counter seats; diners in 2026 were split on the strong, slightly smoky soup.

roles: owner-chef
former manager of 武道家 Kichijōji (about 10 years)
chef_bio.background: Joined Budōka as a teenager, became manager of its Kichijōji shop at the end of his 26th year and ran it for about ten years. He went independent through Mujaki Foods' "Toranavi" trust system, which covers the full opening cost and lets individuals open in areas they could not otherwise afford; Ginza was the location offered.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「庶民が普段使いできる銀座。それを目指します」; and at the door, as in Kichijōji: 「いってらっしゃい」「おかえり」「またね」「また明日」.
chef_bio.specialty: Budōka-style dark pork-bone iekei with chicken oil; nori-wrapped rice.

anecdotes.text: 「武道家に入ったのが10代の頃で、初日からいきなり大将に怒鳴られたんです」
「武道家ベースの濃厚な茶褐色のスープに、鶏油を合わせてまろやかさを足して…麺とスープが絡んで、別々にならない最高の一杯を作ろうとしています」 — before opening.
Walking through Kichijōji, people call out "Ah, you're George, right?" — the press release on the manager regulars came to see.
October 2026: a regular of the Budōka chain wrote that it "definitely carries on the signature richness of Budoka… a bit milder, but that makes it even better."

tokyo_shinamen_hashigo_honten.gf_detail: Not gluten-free. The dandanmen are thin wheat noodles, the signature pāikō version adds a fried pork cutlet, and gyoza and fried spare ribs are on the menu. No gluten-free option is mentioned.
tokyo_shinamen_hashigo_honten.vegan_detail: Not vegan. The dandanmen comes topped with pork (a fried cutlet or thick-cut pork) in a sesame soup whose stock is not described; fried spare ribs and gyoza are the sides.
tokyo_shinamen_hashigo_honten.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–05:00 (next morning); Sat, Sun & holidays 11:00–21:00 (Tabelog). Cash only. Order at your seat.
tokyo_shinamen_hashigo_honten.notes: [Ramen · dandanmen, late night] The main shop of 支那麺 はしご, whose 'dandanmen' (its name for tantanmen) is a Ginza late-night institution: a 2026 diner remembers ending nights out at either Hashigo or the Nagahama stall Yamachan. Since August 2009 this Ginza 6-chōme counter has been the main shop, taking over from the old one in the Ginza Toshiba Building; the brand has more Ginza shops and one in Ningyōchō. The bowl is thin noodles in a nutty sesame soup with moderate heat, a lift of yuzu and a faint curry note. Regulars order pāikō dandanmen with a fried pork cutlet, about ¥1,200 in 2026, with rice to finish the soup, plus beer, fried spare ribs, gyoza and pickled mustard greens. Weekday lunch queues of twenty move fast. Order after you sit; cash only.

chef_bio.origin: This site became the main shop in August 2009 (Tabelog); opening date listed 1 June 2009
chef_bio.background: Tabelog says the former main shop in the Ginza Toshiba Building B1F (Ginza 5-2-1) was merged into this location in August 2009. Other はしご shops are in Ginza 8-chōme, Ginza 4-chōme and Ningyōchō. No source names the operator or founding year.

A diner who usually eats at the Ningyōchō shop found the original looked the same but tasted different.

tokyo_ginza_ton_box.notes: [Ramen · pork chintan] A seven-seat counter opened October 2025 on the side street between the Corridor and old Dentsū-dōri that diners now call a ramen street. tokyo_ramen_shiryu_higashiginza.notes: [Ramen · build your own] A single-storey ramen house near Ginza 3-chōme that says its ramen took ten years to perfect. The soup is pork knuckle and chicken feet boiled over a fierce flame; the noodles are kneaded with wheat bran for flavour and bounce. You choose back fat, garlic, noodle width (thin or medium-thick) and firmness, chashu (pork belly or loin), and three of ten toppings: seasoned egg, menma, nori, wood ear, white onion, green onion, spinach, spicy miso, meat sauce or extra vegetables (five with the 極 bowl, ¥1,100 in 2026). Free rice with lunch, draft beer, and gyoza with house soy or miso sauces. Some diners find it close to Jirō-style when loaded with garlic and fat.

tokyo_nagahama_yatai_yamachan_ginza.notes: [Ramen · Hakata Nagahama] The Tokyo outpost of やまちゃん, a Fukuoka business founded in 1986 as a street stall (yatai) and now shops in Tenjin and Nakasu plus this one in Ginza. The company says it moved from stall to shop without losing the yatai style. In Tokyo the menu stays centred on ramen: a milky pork-bone soup that the company describes as rich but clean and free of smell, thin noodles ordered by firmness (hard, extra hard or soft), and extra noodles. Under a red lantern and noren, it is a classic end to a Higashi-Ginza night, open until 4 a.m.; a 2026 diner remembers ending nights at Yamachan or Hashigo. Hakata-mori with toppings ¥1,400; negi bokkoshi, spicy noodles, vinegared offal, draft beer, and a free small rice at lunch.

The brand belongs to Grand Cuisine, whose Keisuke shops date from 2005 and build 'ramen as cuisine' from Japanese and French technique, each brand on one theme (miso, shoyu, chicken paitan and more). About eight counter seats and two tables for four; diners describe a calm, Japanese-restaurant feel amid the ramen queues of the street.

tokyo_vegan_marshmallooow_ginza_mitsukos.vegan_detail: Fully vegan. A New York-born vegan sweets brand that uses no milk, butter or eggs: soy-milk cream, rice oil, and plant ingredients only. Some main products are also halal-certified.

tokyo_vegan_marshmallooow_ginza_mitsukos.notes: [Fully vegan · some GF · takeaway] A permanent counter of THE VG MARSHMALLOOOW NEW YORK's vegan sweets brand on the B2 sweets floor of Ginza Mitsukoshi. It began as a pop-up in 2021, when medallists from the Tokyo Olympics came by, and went permanent in August 2022. More than thirty sweets are always on offer, the brand says the largest vegan range in Japan, made with no milk, butter or eggs, using soy-milk cream and rice oil. Many are also gluten-free: rice-and-soy-flour sponges for whole zuccotto cakes sold on the day, rice-flour tart cases for seasonal fruit tarts, and a Mont Blanc of Kumamoto chestnut. The cacao-mass Fort Chocolat uses no oil at all. Seasonal cakes for Christmas and Mother's Day are taken by reservation. Not every item is gluten-free, so read the labels.

A FindMeGlutenFree reviewer showed a celiac card and was "reassured that they can prepare gluten free tonkatsu", and users there list pork ribs as gluten-free. The shop publishes nothing about gluten, so how that tonkatsu is coated and fried is unknown. Ordinary tonkatsu is coated in wheat breadcrumbs. Also on the menu: katsu curry, which has a wheat-based roux, and ramen. Treat it as unconfirmed until the shop tells you how it makes a gluten-free cutlet.

The walls are papered with menus in Japanese and English. Loin and fillet katsu sets run about ¥1,300–1,500, katsu curry about ¥1,650–1,700, and there is eel and ramen too. Diners give a ¥300 repeat coupon and cheerful service good marks, the batter and meat less so. On FindMeGlutenFree, one reviewer with a celiac card was told the kitchen can make a gluten-free tonkatsu. Nothing from the shop confirms how, so ask about the coating and the fryer before you order.

chef_bio.specialty: Loin katsu sets; katsu curry; eel.

anecdotes.text: FindMeGlutenFree featured review: "Stopped in and showed them my celiac card and they reassured me that they can prepare gluten free tonkatsu!"
A first visit earns a ¥300-off coupon for the next one, which one regular says takes the edge off Ginza tourist pricing.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 銀座とんかつ はし勝つ、銀座3-12-1、2023年10月6日オープン、7席、月〜金11:00〜18:00、土11:30〜15:00、日祝休、カード・交通系IC・PayPay可、弁当のみ予約可。口コミ: 元はんこ屋、壁向きカウンター、英語メニュー、ロースかつ定食1,300〜1,500円、カツカレー1,650〜1,700円、うなぎ・ラーメン、次回300円引き券。FindMeGlutenFree: 口コミ8件、「セリアックのカードを見せたら、グルテンフリーのとんかつを作れると言われた」。

cultural_comfort.note: English and romanised menus on the walls; seven counter seats facing the wall. Cards, IC and PayPay accepted.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Ordinary breaded tonkatsu and katsu curry from the same small kitchen.
